name: A Nonpeelable Overlap of a Forbidden Expansion Is Itself Forbidden
statement: Let $H$ be an ample forbidden pc-minor and let $A=H^{\{e\}}$ be its full reduction in an active coordinate. If $A$ is not dismantlable ample, then $A$ is itself an ample forbidden pc-minor. Repeating this descent terminates at an obstruction whose full reduction in every active coordinate is dismantlable ample. Each inverse step canonically recovers $H=(A\times\{0,1\})\cup(R_0\times\{0\})\cup(R_1\times\{1\})$, with nonempty signed wings and with both sections and their union dismantlable ample.
proof: Restriction and contraction in any other coordinate commute with full reduction on ample families. Applying full-reduction closure to the corresponding proper pc-minor of H shows that every elementary pc-minor of A is dismantlable ample. Thus a nonpeelable A is forbidden. Each step removes a coordinate, so descent terminates; the two-cone dichotomy makes every terminal coordinate gluing-critical. Periphery-freeness makes both inverse wings nonempty, and the sections and their union are proper pc-minors of H.
comments: The overlap is a full reduction and need not itself be a pc-minor of the original family.
